newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money steady in early trade, gilts up.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money steady in early trade, gilts up.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted at 1.5-2.0 percent in early trade Friday, marginally up from Thursday's close of 1.0-1/5 percent, dealers said.
They said the announcement of a government bond auction on Thursday had little impact and rates remained easy.
The government on Thursday announced a 30 billion rupee auction of six-year bonds for July 16.

"Normally the fear of liquidity being sucked out of the banking system leads to a tightening of rates and security prices fall a bit," said a dealer. "But this auction has been anticipated for some time and its effect discounted, call is little changed and security prices up."
"Stocks are being quoted at least 10 paise higher already," the dealer said.
Dealers said they expected prices of government securities to go up in active trade on Friday.
